injuries.detail: Froholdt appeared on Arizona's injury report with a concussion Wednesday, and now his status for Week 10 is in serious doubt. If he can't return to practice Friday and advance through the NFL's five-step concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game versus the Rams, he'll have to miss his first regular-season contest since he joined the Cardinals back in 2023.

Williams was sidelined for Arizona's game at Seattle in Week 9 due to a knee injury, and it's evidently still hindering him ahead of Sunday's game versus the Rams. Unless he can manage a full practice Friday, he'll likely end up taking an injury designation into the weekend.

Wingard was limited in Wednesday's practice. However, he wasn't on the field for Thursday's session, so things don't look promising regarding his availability in Week 10 against the Rams. The 29-year-old is coming off a 12-tackle performance in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. If Wingard can't suit up Sunday, Kitan Crawford and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson are candidates for more snaps.

Knight was limited Wednesday after donning a yellow non-contact jersey in practice, but after ditching it one day later, he was able to handle every on-field rep. That's not to say he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires an evaluation from an independent neurologist, but he's likely on the precipice of doing so. Friday's injury report will determine if Knight heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.
questionable

The star safety has now logged three 11-tackle games this season, and Baker remains one of the bright spots for a Cardinals team that doesn't have many in 2026. The 10th-year pro was mentioned in trade rumors prior to Tuesday's deadline, but he'll finish out the campaign in Arizona. He's up to 62 tackles (29 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. Baker appears headed for an eighth straight Pro Bowl selection.

Carter opened the season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained during training camp. He was a limited practice participant in Wednesday's session, but he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Rams.

The tight end was injured in Week 4 against the Giants but had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday. Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano have been soaking up the snaps at the position behind Trey McBride in recent weeks.

Arizona first dealt Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore last Friday, and then Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right elbow during this past Sunday's game at Seattle and will undergo season-ending surgery. That series of events precedes Beck taking over as the Cards' No. 1 signal-caller, and with eight other skill-position players on reserve lists at the moment, the top talents available to the offense will be TE Trey McBride and RB Tyler Allgeier.
With Minshew already on injured reserve, the surgery confirms he won't return for Arizona this season. Carson Beck is now Arizona's starting QB for Week 11 against the Rams and beyond.

Ten of Hull's 12 snaps came on special teams, and he wasn't bale to connect with Gardner Minshew on the latter's pass attempt early in the third quarter. Hull has yet to log a carry through three regular-season appearances with the Cardinals. However, he could operate as the team's RB2 behind Tyler Allgeier for Week 10 against the Rams if Bam Knight doesn't clear the league's concussion protocol for that contest.

Fehoko has already climbed way up the wideout pecking order over the past two weeks, logging a 49 percent offensive snap share in both games after not exceeding a 12 percent snap share through the first seven weeks. However, the veteran wideout hasn't been able to do much with the recent opportunity, and he's stuck on one catch for 17 yards on two targets through nine contests. With that said, somebody is going to have to step up in the wideout corps to try to replace the production of Michael Wilson (neck), Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist), all of whom have been lost to season-ending injuries over the past two weeks. Fehoko is a candidate to take on some of that responsibility along with Reggie Virgil, Devin Duvernay and Harrison Wallace. The Cardinals will also be working with a new quarterback moving forward, as rookie Carson Beck is lined up to claim the starting role from Gardner Minshew (elbow), who landed on injured reserve Tuesday.

Gardner Minshew found Virgil for a 25-yard pass early in the first quarter, but the duo failed to connect for the rest of Sunday's contest. The Cardinals' offense took some big hits in Week 9, with Minshew sustaining a torn UCL and wide receiver Michael Wilson suffering a fracture in his neck, and those injuries will keep both players on the shelf for the rest of the 2026 season. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are both also on season-ending IR, which leaves Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and superstar tight end Trey McBride as the top targets for rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck heading into Week 10 against the Rams.

With all of the injuries at wide receiver for Arizona, Higgins played a season-high 66 percent of the offensive snaps in Seattle. It still didn't translate to an elevated role in the pass game. Higgins has 18 grabs for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets across nine games this season.

A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.

Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three carries across his nine appearances.

Arizona has yet to announce a corresponding move, but top quarterback Gardner Minshew could be headed to injured reserve after sustaining a torn ACL in Sunday's loss to the Seahawks that may require season-ending surgery. An undrafted rookie out of Tennessee, Aguilar joins fellow rookie Carson Beck and veteran journeyman Josh Johnson as the healthy options in the Cardinals' quarterback room. Aguilar will likely settle in as the No. 3 option on the depth chart if Minshew is indeed placed on IR.

Ryland played just three snaps during the loss, though he managed to convert his only kick, which came from 28 yards and also served as the team's only points in the game. He now has converted 20 of his 22 field-goal attempts and 16 of his 17 extra-point tries across nine games this season.

Johnson will head to Arizona in what will mark the 15th different NFL organization that he's been a part of since entering the league as a fifth-round pick in 2008. The 40-year-old is expected to operate as the primary backup option behind rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who is poised to make his first NFL start Week 10 versus the Rams in place of the injured Gardner Minshew (elbow). With Minshew at risk of missing the remainder of the 2026 campaign while he recovers from a torn UCL, Johnson will likely stick around Arizona until the season concludes.

Daniels was also limited by an Achilles injury during the Thursday of Week 8 prep. He ultimately avoided an injury designation for that game against the Buccaneers and played without limitations in Week 9 against the Bengals as well. The rookie fourth-round pick's availability for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will be clarified on Friday's injury report.
questionable

Williams was placed on IR before Atlanta's regular-season opener with an ankle injury, but he's now finally back to full strength following Week 9. Starting in Week 10, he projects to fill a depth role at tackle behind veteran Jake Matthews and offseason free-agent acquisition Jawaan Taylor.

The rookie wideout was injured in the Week 8 loss to the Bucs and missed last Sunday's loss to the Bengals in Spain. Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair picked up extra snaps behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson.

Herbert continued to serve a limited role in his first game since being signed to the active roster from the practice squad, as he played just 11 snaps on offense and nine on special teams. With Brian Robinson (hamstring) set to miss at least another three games, Herbert will likely continue to serve as the team's backup running back behind Bijan Robinson.

Zaccheaus briefly left Sunday's game and was evaluated for a possible concussion, but the veteran wide receiver was quickly cleared to return. He has only six catches (on 16 targets) for 26 yards through eight regular-season games, and he's caught one pass or zero in seven of those contests. Zaccheaus isn't a key piece in the Falcons' offense, and that's unlikely to change heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs on Nov. 15.

Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.

The move gives the Falcons additional depth at the guard position behind starters Chris Lindstrom and Matthew Bergeron. Vorhees -- a seventh-round selection of the Ravens in the 2023 NFL Draft -- started in all 17 regular-season games in 2025, but he's started in only two of five contests this year. He also missed two games in October while recovering from a foot injury.

It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.

It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

Abdullah was placed on injured reserve Oct. 10 due to a hamstring injury, and after missing the required four games while on the list, he was designated to return Wednesday and then activated Saturday, setting him up for his first game action since Week 4. A rotational role off the edge is likely for Abdullah due to James Pearce (back) making his season debut and all of Cameron Thomas, Za'Darius Smith and Charles Snowden available to the defense.

On cutdown day Aug. 30, the Falcons placed Collins on IR with a designation to return, which would have allowed him to practice as early as Week 3 prep. Instead, his hip injury kept him out of drills until Week 7, when his 21-day window opened, but he sat out the last two games before Atlanta finally activated him Saturday. With Zachariah Branch sidelined Sunday due to a hamstring issue, Collins will serve as a reserve WR along with Chris Blair behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.

Robinson already has missed two games due to a lingering hamstring injury and now must miss at least the next four outings, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Dec. 13 at Cleveland. In a corresponding move, the Falcons are signing Khalil Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster to continue serving as the No. 2 RB behind workhorse Bijan Robinson.

Ebukam suffered a hamstring injury in Week 9 versus the Buccaneers, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result of the injury. In his absence, Za'Darius Smith is a top candidate to operate in a more prominent role at outside linebacker.

Blair has been active for all eight of the Falcons' games this season, but the 29-year-old wideout has been scarcely involved on offense. He's thus far recorded just a six-yard reception on four targets, three of which came in Week 2. Blair should continue to suit up for the Falcons on gamedays but will provide most of his value on special teams.

Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was recently acquired from the Cardinals, figures to hold down the starting quarterback spot in Jackson's absence.

Hamilton suffered a hip injury during the Week 9 loss to Jacksonville and didn't finish the contest. Now, after logging a full practice Thursday, he is good to go for Monday's game against the Chargers, assuming he doesn't suffer a setback along the way. Hamilton has appeared in all nine games for Baltimore during the 2026 campaign, accumulating 60 total tackles (43 solo), one interception and five passes defended.

Wiggins was inactive for the Week 9 meeting with the Jaguars. However, after logging a full practice session Thursday, it appears he is good to go for Week 10 against the Chargers. The 23-year-old has appeared in eight games this season, garnering 24 total tackles (17 solo) and four passes defensed.

Hawkins missed the last three games due to a knee injury. While he practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, he likely has some hurdles to clear before getting the green light to suit up Monday night against the Chargers. If Hawkins can't play, K'Von Wallace should continue to see more snaps.

Bateman now has two more opportunities to practice fully and thus avoid an injury designation prior to Monday night's game against the Chargers. The starting wideout is coming off back-to-back one-catch efforts, but he'll perhaps have an opportunity to bounce back against 0-8 Los Angeles, while working with a new QB in Jacoby Brissett.
questionable

The Ravens signed Harrison Mevis to their practice squad in addition to signing Patterson to the 53-man roster, but the team intends to utilize Patterson as the kicker for Monday's game. Patterson went 7-for-9 on field-goal attempts in five appearances with the Dolphins this season, with a long of just 41 yards. His career-long made field goal of 54 yards came with Miami last season.

Neuzil had started at center in each of the Falcons' first nine games of the season, but he's expected to fill a more versatile backup role in Baltimore, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. In addition to center, Neuzil is capable of playing both guard spots, so he'll likely be the top candidate to start if Cam Jurgens, John Simpson or Vega Ioane misses time at any point.

Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.

Starks tied for third on his team in tackles during a rather uninspiring performance on both offense and defense by the Ravens. He did make a big play when he forced a fumble that was recovered by Baltimore in the third quarter, but the Ravens turned the ball over on downs on four plays on their ensuing possession. Starks logged 84 tackles over 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, and he's well on his way to surpassing that mark with 55 stops (including 1.0 sacks) through nine contests in 2026.

Smith led his team in tackles on a night when Baltimore had a hard time slowing down the Jaguars' offense. Though he's been bothered by knee and foot issues in recent weeks, the veteran linebacker logged a 95 percent defensive snap share Thursday. Smith is well on his way to another triple-digit tackle campaign with 74 stops, including 2.0 sacks, along with an interception and two forced fumbles through nine contests.

With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.

Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.

Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.

Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.

The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.

Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly putting the finishing touches on a trade with the Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, Fagnano is likely to move into a reserve role as soon as a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

Isaac is nursing a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. The linebacker operates primarily as a special-teams option, so his absence doesn't have any impact on Baltimore's defensive approach.
questionable

Kincaid has opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. He has faced plenty of practice limitations throughout the season, but Kincaid has yet to sit out a game. That pattern seems unlikely to change in Week 10 against the Jets.

The ball-hawking linebacker picked off Carson Wentz in the third quarter and almost got another pick later in the second half. Bernard has at least one interception in each of the last four regular seasons and has seven total in that span. Across eight games, all starts, this season, Bernard has logged 57 tackles (29 solo), three pass breakups, including the interception, and a fumble recovery on 91 percent of Buffalo's defensive snaps.

A rib injury prevented Dawkins from playing against the Vikings on Monday. He has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets. Tylan Grable would likely start at left tackle if Dawkins is unable to play.

Gaines missed the Bills' last two games while recovering from a calf injury, but his full session Wednesday indicates that he'll return for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Jets. He's accumulated 11 tackles (three solo) and one fumble recovery through six regular-season games, and his return gives the Bills additional depth on the defensive line.

Benford injured his wrist in Monday night's win over the Vikings but was able to return to the contest. Across seven starts this season, he has 31 tackles (21 solo) and seven pass breakups on 89 percent of the defensive snaps.
questionable
questionable

Latu gave the Bills the lead late in the first half when he got open in the back of the end zone and caught a pass from Josh Allen. It was not only his first catch of the campaign but also his first NFL touchdown. Latu has worked primarily on special teams this season, and despite his score Monday, he isn't likely to suddenly be a big part of the passing game given the fact that Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes all remain ahead of him on the tight-end depth chart.

Hawes played a season-high 46 snaps on offense and also played eight snaps on special teams. The 25-year-old has now caught a pass in consecutive games after failing to record any receptions across his first six outings of the campaign.

Bass opened Monday's scoring with a 39-yard field goal in the first quarter before converting on kicks from 25 and 52 yards in the second half. All three of his 50-plus yard field goals this season have come over his last two outings, and he's made all 19 of his field-goal attempts and 23 of 25 PAT's through eight regular-season games. Bass's scoring floor is one of the highest in the NFL given the Bills' juggernaut offense led by MVP candidate Josh Allen. They'll hit the road for Week 10 in an AFC East tilt against the Jets on Nov. 15.

Knox's targets, catches and yards were all season highs. He also played 58 offensive snaps against Minnesota. With the blitz-happy Vikings defense opposite them, the Buffalo offense went with heavy tight end sets to try and get more blockers on the field. Knox won't be a recommended fantasy target for Sunday's game against the Jets. He has 13 grabs for 79 yards and a touchdown across eight games this season.

Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.

Johnson got just one carry while workhorse No. 1 RB James Cook logged a hearty 31 totes. However, Johnson made one big play as a receiver, hauling in a 36-yard reception on a third-down play early in the third quarter to bring Buffalo into Vikings territory. While Johnson has been nearly invisible as a ball carrier this season, he's been effective in a pass-catching role, racking up 210 yards on 17 catches through six games.

Shakir tied for the team lead in receptions while setting the pace in receiving yards on a night when Josh Allen spread the ball around to eight different targets. The veteran receiver continues to maintain his trademark steady presence in Buffalo's air attack, now having recorded at least Monday night's catch and yardage tallies in four of the last five games. Shakir carries a bright outlook into a Week 10 road matchup against a vulnerable Jets defense on Sunday.

Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.

The veteran receiver came into the game without an injury designation related to the shoulder issue he's managing, but Moore still put together a modest performance against a tough Vikings defense that kept pressure on Josh Allen throughout the night. Moore has a combined 7-107-1 line on on 12 targets in the two contests he's suited up for since returning from a two-game absence, and he should have a much better chance of downfield success in a Week 10 road matchup against the Jets' vulnerable defense Sunday.

Allen came into the night undoubtedly expecting to have to work for everything he got, and Brian Flores' aggressive defensive unit helped validate that prognosis by sacking the star signal-caller on four occasions. However, Allen was able to navigate the dangers pretty effectively, spreading the ball around to eight different targets overall. He connected with Keleki Latu from 25 yards out late in the first half for his one touchdown pass, and Allen's lone turnover, a first-quarter interception on a deep shot in the Vikings' end zone, didn't lead to any Minnesota points. Allen hasn't eclipsed the 300-yard threshold since Week 1, but he'll take 2,027 passing yards and a 12:6 TD:INT alongside 285 rushing yards into a Week 10 road divisional clash against the Jets on Sunday.

Cook was repeatedly stonewalled through three quarters by a Vikings run defense that had been fairly beatable, but the star running back continued to get opportunities to test Minnesota's defensive front. That approach finally began paying off on an early fourth-quarter marathon scoring drive, one where Cook recorded runs of nine, six and 11 yards before capping off the march with a five-yard scoring rush to extend Buffalo's 13-6 lead. Cook ultimately fell just a carry short of tying his career high, and he eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the fourth time this season. The fifth-year pro's trip to the end zone extended his touchdown streak to seven games as well, and Cook will head into a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Jets just 186 rushing yards short of his fourth straight 1,000-yard campaign.
Hamlin is back in the game after having briefly exited while dealing with cramping. Geno Stone had replaced Hamlin at safety while he was sidelined.

Anderson is dealing with an ankle injury that caused him to miss practice Thursday and Friday. He was able to log a limited session Saturday, but that won't be enough for him to suit up for Monday Night Football. Austin Corbett figures to start at left guard in Anderson's place.

Shavers will remain sidelined for at least one more game as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL. The wide receiver returned to practice in late October, and he could be activated prior to the team's Week 10 matchup with the Jets.

The Panthers listed Legette as a full participant Wednesday on their estimated practice report. He gets the same listing after an actual practice and seems to be closing in on a return from injured reserve. Carolina would need to activate Legette by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have him on the roster for Sunday's game at New Orleans. Legette was Carolina's No. 3 receiver earlier this season, and neither John Metchie nor Brycen Tremayne has made much of an impact in his absence.

The Panthers also listed Brooks as 'FP' on Wednesday's estimated practice report. Now that he's actually logged a full practice, Brooks may have a real shot to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game at New Orleans. The Panthers would need to make that move by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Brooks on the active roster Sunday.

Okereke was estimated as a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough, and he remained sidelined for Thursday's full-speed practice. Barring a return to practice Friday, Okereke could be in line for a second consecutive absence Sunday against the Saints after he racked up 49 tackles (31 solo) through his first seven games with the Panthers.

Lloyd played every single defensive snap and co-led the Panthers in tackles with Tyrel Dodson. It was the fifth time this season that Lloyd has logged at least seven combined tackles, and the fifth-year pro is up to 54 stops (32 solo), including 2.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception and a pick-six) across seven regular-season games.

Lewis has missed the Panthers' last two games due to a knee injury, but his full session Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's NFC South tilt against the Saints. His return gives the Panthers more depth at offensive guard behind starters Robert Hunt and Torricelli Simpkins.

Lee missed last Sunday's loss to the Broncos after he was injured 10 days prior in the Week 8 loss to the Packers. Marco Wilson and Corey Thornton handled most of the cornerback snaps in Week 9 against Denver, but Lee appears ready to return to action.

Phillips has missed the last three games for Carolina, but he appears to be ready to return to the field Sunday versus New Orleans. Across five games this season, Phillips has produced 10 tackles (three solo), including 2.5 sacks.

Jackson was placed on injured reserve late in September after suffering a groin injury in Week 3 against Cleveland. The 29-year-old's potential return would greatly help a depleted Carolina secondary, which lost both Jackson and Jaycee Horn (quadriceps) early in the season. Jackson has five tackles (three solo) in his two full regular-season games.

Both of Metchie's receptions came in the second half -- he brought in a 15-yarder midway through the third quarter and added a 25-yarder near the end of the fourth. The latter catch took the ball down to Denver's nine-yard line and set up a Panthers touchdown, but Carolina ultimately was unable to complete the comeback. Metchie has been consistent but relatively unremarkable this season, logging either two or three receptions in six straight games but not surpassing Sunday's 40 yards in any of those contests.

For the third game in a row, Evans drew exactly two targets and caught both of them Sunday. With that said, he also again trailed in snaps at tight end (31) behind teammates Tommy Tremble (46) and Darren Waller (35), both of whom also drew more targets in Week 9. Evans' role in the Panthers' passing offense isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats going into a Week 10 matchup at New Orleans.

Etienne once again saw limited action offensively, playing just seven snaps. The 2025 fourth-round pick was the only running back other than Chuba Hubbard to record a carry and should continue to serve as the team's No. 2 back while Jonathon Brooks remains sidelined due to an abdomen injury.

Fitzgerald went without a field-goal make for the second time in three weeks, and he pushed his only field-goal attempt of the day wide right from 43 yards in the second quarter. The miss was his first on a field-goal try this year, and the kicker now has gone 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, while making 16 of 21 extra-point attempts over eight regular-season contests so far.

Horn has had a productive NFL career, amassing 196 total tackles (139 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and 10 interceptions across 56 regular-season games over six seasons. He underwent surgery on his quad back in September. However, until Horn is back on the field or there is a more informative update, he should be considered week-to-week.

Sanders was active for the first time this season. However, he didn't log any offensive snaps and spent all his time on special teams. The 23-year-old has appeared in 30 regular-season games during his career, amassing 62 catches (77 targets) for 532 yards and two touchdowns. Sanders has had a few quality performances throughout his short NFL career, though he likely won't have an opportunity to get involved offensively moving ahead while Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller are in the mix.

It was yet another quiet game from Coker, who has been held below 40 receiving yards in four of the last five games. Since his massive 8-138-2 receiving line in Week 1, Coker has averaged just 3.8 catches for 65.5 receiving yards per game over his last six contests. He has only one touchdown during that span. Coker will be in a bounce-back spot against the Saints at the Superdome next Sunday.

The Panthers continue to use three tight ends heavily on offense, and Tremble has settled in as the do-it-all tight member of the trio, while Darren Waller is solely a pass catcher and Mitchell Evans focuses on blocking. Tremble doesn't have nearly the upside of Waller, but the former still draws Bryce Young's eye in the red zone. On the year, Tremble is up to 21 grabs for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 30 targets across eight games. He's not an exciting fantasy option.

The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.

The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.

The 27-year-old RB nearly produced 100-plus scrimmage yards for the fifth time in the last six games but fell just short. Hubbard remains on track for a career-best campaign, and through eight games he's delivered 619 yards and five TDs on the ground while adding a 26-167-2 line on 31 targets. He lines up for a juicy matchup in Week 10 against the Saints.

The fourth-year QB tossed TDs in each of the last three quarters, finding Tommy Tremble, Darren Waller and Tetairoa McMillan, but Young's attempt to engineer a game-winning drive inside the final two minutes ended on a Nik Bonitto strip sack. It's the third time this season Young has thrown three touchdowns, but his first such performance since Week 2. He'll take a 16:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Saints.
Simpkins didn't suit up in the Week 8 loss to Green Bay due to an ankle injury, though it won't keep him off the field again for Sunday's meeting with the Broncos.
Bullock was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. However, after logging full sessions Thursday and Friday, he is good to go for Week 9.

In a game that featured seven turnovers between the two teams, Johnson's takeaway was arguably the most impactful of them all. He jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Cade Otton late in the third quarter, which Johnson returned 67 yards to the house for the second pick-six of his NFL career. The veteran defensive back is up to 27 tackles (21 solo), three pass defenses (including a pick-six) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

Lewis jumped in front of a Baker Mayfield pass intended for Tez Johnson late in the second quarter, although the Bears offense turned the ball over on the very next play. It was the first interception of the season for Lewis and second of his career. The veteran safety is up to 35 tackles (25 solo) and two pass defenses across eight regular-season games.

Simmons took down Baker Mayfield for a three-yard sack midway through the fourth quarter, which was one of four sacks that the Bears recorded in Week 9. Simmons has logged sacks in back-to-back games in his first two outings with the Bears, and for the regular season, he is up to 48 tackles (26 solo), including 6.0 sacks, six pass defenses, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery across nine games.

Thomas continues to see limited action offensively, playing just five snaps Sunday and no more than 15 on offense in any game this season, though he did manage to record his seventh reception of the season. The rookie third-round pick should continue to see the majority of his action come on special teams, and he's now amassed 715 kick-return yards across nine outings this season.

Roush, who has been utilized heavily as a blocker through nine games, achieved a new career high in receiving yards in Week 9. Roush has been relatively efficient with his limited targets so far this season, but Colston Loveland should be expected to continue to handle a substantial majority of the Bears' pass-catching duties at tight end as long as he's available.

Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was inactive for a fifth consecutive game, with Johnson operating as the Bears' RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in the Bears' four contests prior to Sunday against the Bucs. However, Johnson didn't play a single offensive snap against Tampa Bay; instead, it was Salvon Ahmed (five carries for 25 yards) who mixed into the backfield as Chicago's complementary piece to Swift. The Bears are on a bye for Week 10, with their next game taking place in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22. Johnson would have a narrow path to offensive relevancy if Monangai is cleared to return for that contest.

Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye in Week 10.

It was an up-and-down night for Chicago's offense Sunday, as it moved the ball relatively well but committed five turnovers. Nevertheless, Santos got an opportunity to win the game on the last play of regulation with a 38-yard field goal, and it looked good from the moment it left his foot. Following a bye in Week 10, the Bears will play host to the Saints in Week 11, at which point fantasy managers might want to confirm the weather forecast in Chicago before locking Santos back into their lineups.

Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.

Swift was bottled up by an elite Buccaneers run defense that came into Week 9 allowing a league-low 80 rushing yards per game. He nearly had a fumble in the fourth quarter but was ruled down by contact on a play that the Buccaneers unsuccessfully challenged. Swift's momentum came to an abrupt halt with this season-worst performance, as he failed to reach 70 scrimmage yards for the first time all season after racking up seven touchdowns in the preceding four games. After Chicago's Week 10 bye, Swift could be back to sharing the backfield with Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who hasn't played since Week 4 but recently returned to practice.

Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.
With Stevenson sidelined and Malik Muhammad (toe) inactive, Josh Blackwell and Clark Phillips will take on more defensive snaps alongside Jaylon Phillips and Kyler Gordon at cornerback for the Bears.

Muhammad was expected to be able to return to action in Week 9, but the cornerback will now be forced to miss a second straight game while nursing a toe injury he suffered in Week 7. In his absence, Josh Blackwell is a top candidate to see an increase in opportunities at cornerback behind starters Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson versus the Buccaneers.

Keenum will once again operate as the team's emergency QB option in Week 9, making it four games in a row in that role. The 38-year-old will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Caleb Williams and backup Tyson Bagent are forced out of the contest.

Monangai finally was able to mix into drills Friday for the first time since emerging from Week 4 with a turf-toe injury, going down as a limited participant. The Bears kept the door open for him to return by giving him a questionable designation, but after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Monangai isn't expected to play in Week 9, his inactive status doesn't come as a surprise. However, Rapoport also noted that Monangai is on pace to be back in Week 11 versus the Saints following a Week 10 bye. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will be Chicago's lead runner, with Roschon Johnson backing him up.

After missing the Bears' walk-through practice Wednesday, Jarrett logged a limited practice Thursday and then upgraded again to a full practice Friday. He should start on the interior of the defensive line next to Jeffery Simmons again in Week 9.

injuries.evidence: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games.
injuries.detail: Scott will be required to miss at least the next four games. He's appeared in four contests this season, playing 65 snaps on special teams.

injuries.evidence: He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season.
injuries.detail: Street was injured in Monday night's win over the Seahawks and had to be carted to the locker room. He's now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season. Fellow DT Grady Jarrett (groin) was also injured in Seattle, making the move for Jeffery Simmons that much more important for Chicago.

injuries.evidence: Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
injuries.detail: Jones underwent right knee surgery Tuesday, and as a result, he will be forced to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign. In his absence, Theo Benedet (shoulder) will continue to operate as the team's primary option at left tackle.

Turner was able to play through his ankle injury in Week 9 against the Falcons, and it now looks like it's behind him entirely. He projects to start at cornerback against a pass-heavy Steelers offense Sunday.

Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.

Davis was placed on injured reserve in late September after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals now have 21 days to officially activate the 30-year-old for him to remain eligible to play this season.

Iosivas, who landed on IR on Sept. 26, is bouncing back from surgery to repair a torn ligament in his thumb, and the wideout's looming return to Thursday's practice has him trending the right direction ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers. Once he's back in action, Iosivas will slot back in behind top WRs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, a role that doesn't typically yield steady volume.

Cook had his most productive outing of the campaign, logging a season-high 10 tackles. The 2022 second-round pick will look to build on this performance and keep producing during the team's Week 10 matchup versus the Steelers.

Carter had one of his most productive outings of the season during the victory, as he matched Bryan Cook for the most tackles on the team in addition to recording his first interception of the campaign. The 2025 fourth-round pick has racked up 68 tackles (28 solo), including 1.5 sacks, an interception and two forced fumbles across eight games this season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Steelers.

Dugger has been sidelined by a quadriceps injury for the Bengals' last two games, and he has not been cleared to return to practice. He would likely need to practice in at least a limited fashion over the next two days in order to have a realistic chance of playing against the Steelers on Sunday.

With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, Meyers has settled in as the Bengals' third receiver behind target hogs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers would need an injury to one of those two to become relevant again in fantasy.

Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out-produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a modest role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.

McPherson was able to convert multiple field-goal tries in a game for the first time since Week 3, nailing a 57-yarder in the final moments of the first half before later adding a 43-yard make in the fourth quarter. The kicker had gone back-to-back games without a field-goal attempt, but he has now gone a perfect 12-for-12 on field-goal tries, including 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests this season.

Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.

Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.

The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

Johnson suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus the Titans, and he subsequently followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen during Week 9 prep before getting a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's international matchup. Now that he's confirmed to be active, he should be good for his normal 20-30 percent weekly defensive snap share.

Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.

Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.

Boston has dealt with calf, foot and toe injuries in recent weeks, never missing a game or requiring any workload limitations. He missed back-to-back practices to open this week, but he sounded optimistic Thursday and is now back on the field Friday. It remains to be seen if Boston will get an injury designation on the final report Friday afternoon. The Browns host the Texans on Sunday, facing a talented defense that struggled in the first half of the season and still has injury concerns after a Week 9 bye.

The same applies to Fannin's Wednesday practice participation, but it's worth noting that the tight end also was limited by his groin issue last Thursday and Friday before approaching the Browns' Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints without an injury designation. Friday's injury report will reveal whether that pattern is repeated ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

Harden took down Tyler Shough for 10- and six-yard sacks in the third and fourth quarters, respectively, which were the former's first sacks of his three-year NFL career. The 2024 seventh-rounder is up to 33 tackles (19 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through nine regular-season games.

Schwesinger may have tweaked his wrist during the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9, when he logged a season-high 15 tackles (10 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one forced fumble. He has two more chances to log a full practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

Ward was on the field for 73 of the Browns' 75 defensive snaps in Week 9, and his presence at practice Wednesday suggests his injury is likely not severe. If he can log a full practice Thursday or Friday, there's a solid chance he'll be able to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Williams has been working through a hamstring issue as of late, although he was cleared to play against the Saints in Week 9, when he logged seven tackles (five solo) in a 23-22 overtime loss for the Browns. He's opened Week 10 prep with a limited session, and he has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

Burton suffered a calf injury against the Saints in Week 9. He was cleared to return to that contest, but he's still working through the injury and was held out of Wednesday's practice. Burton will have two more opportunities to practice ahead of Sunday's contest against the Texans.

Hickman suffered a concussion in Week 9 against the Saints. He will have multiple steps to work through, but has the full week to clear concussion protocol. The fourth-year pro has 57 tackles (26 solo), four pass deflections and one interception in nine regular-season games this season.

Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 record over their first eight games before developing concussion symptoms and being placed in the NFL's five-step protocol last week. Though Watson cleared protocol last Saturday, his lack of on-field reps during the week prompted the Browns to keep him inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Saints. Sanders stepped in under center and overcame a slow start to finish with 297 passing yards, 28 rushing yards, two passing touchdowns and no turnovers in a 23-22 overtime loss, with his performance drawing praise from head coach Todd Monken. Though the Browns will go back to a healthy Watson for Week 10, Sanders' strong outing in New Orleans could put Watson on shakier ground atop the depth chart.

Watson cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol this past Saturday, but because he managed just one limited practice during Week 9 prep, the Browns opted to make him inactive for their matchup with the Saints. Shedeur Sanders drew his first start of the season and threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the team's 23-22 overtime loss in New Orleans, but he'll return to the No. 2 role this week while a healthy Watson reclaims the starting job. Though the Browns have gone 5-3 with Watson under center this season, he hasn't been without his flaws (six turnovers, 33 sacks taken). As such, Watson may need a strong showing against the Texans to hold off Sanders for the starting job in the weeks to come.

Szmyt was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the eighth straight game, and his three makes matched a season high for the 28-year-old. The kicker made a 41-yarder in the second quarter and a 30-yard attempt in the third quarter before tying the game up at 16-16 with a 51-yard make with eight seconds left in regulation. Szmyt has now gone 19-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

The veteran wideout had zero grabs headed into the Browns' finals drive of regulation, but a 30-yard grab down the left sideline followed up a by a seven-yard gain two plays later set Cleveland up for the game-tying field goal to send it to overtime. The fourth option in the passing attack for the Browns, Jeudy has 18 catches for 208 yards and no touchdowns through nine games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.

Sampson toted the rock a season-high eight times, but he averaged a minimal 2.6 yards per carry. The running back remained heavily involved in the passing game, tying wide receiver KC Concepcion for second on the team in targets behind wideout Denzel Boston (seven). Sampson has now reeled in three or more passes in three straight games, and he figures to remain most valuable as a pass catcher for fantasy managers ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with Houston.

Most of Concepcion's production came on a 64-yard TD in the fourth quarter as Shedeur Sanders found him just inside New Orleans' 30-yard line and the speedy rookie -- who briefly exited the contest after sustained what appeared to be a right leg issue -- to did the rest by eluding a couple defenders. It was Concepcion's first career NFL touchdown, and he sports a 37-437-1 line on 55 targets through his first nine games for the Browns. If Sanders takes over from Deshaun Watson (concussion) on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays for Concepcion.

The Browns' running game once again struggled, with the team averaging just 2.8 yards per carry overall, and Judkins' longest gain went for only 12 yards. Dylan Sampson saw a season-high 11 touches to Judkins' 16, and the backfield could be drifting toward a timeshare as coach Todd Monken looks for solutions. Judkins has topped 70 rushing yards in a game just once all season, and he seems unlikely to break out in a Week 10 meeting with the Texans.

It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest due to Deshaun Watson being in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.

Pickens didn't play last week but has a chance to avoid further absences. He's been a limited practice participant so far this week, and a 'questionable' designation seems likely heading into the weekend. We'll find out more when the Cowboys release their final injury report Friday afternoon/evening.

Overshown didn't play in the Week 9 win over the Colts. He was limited in Wednesday's practice, though after logging a full session Thursday, he is good to go for Sunday's meeting with the 49ers. The 26-year-old has appeared in only three games during the 2026 campaign, amassing 20 total tackles (eight solo) and one interception.

Mingo didn't practice for a second consecutive day due to foot and ankle issues. He logged a season-high 31 offensive snaps in the narrow win over the Colts in Week 9. Mingo could be busier than usual once again versus the 49ers if KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and George Pickens (hamstring) miss another game. However, Mingo will need to be cleared to suit up for that to happen.

Turpin was limited for a second consecutive practice. He has missed the last three games, and if that trend continues Sunday versus San Francisco, Jonathan Mingo (ankle) and Camden Brown could remain more involved than usual.

Squaring off with his older brother Josh Downs on the opposite side, Downs recorded his first career interception on the Colts' final offensive play of the game with 41 seconds left in the fourth quarter. On a pass intended for Keenan Allen, Downs picked off Daniel Jones to seal the four-point win. The first-round rookie Downs now has 55 tackles (32 solo), including 2.0 sacks, three pass breakups, with the interception, and a pair of forced fumbles on 93 percent of the defensive snaps across nine starts this season.

The Cowboys' top cornerback has appeared in just four games with the team since being acquired from the Steelers ahead of Week 4. He missed last Sunday's win over the Colts, so Cobie Durant made the start opposite DaRon Bland and played all 64 defensive snaps.
The tight end has missed the past two games for Dallas, but appears to be ready to return and could see significant snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford while Jake Ferguson (knee) is sidelined.

The fourth-round rookie cornerback has yet to play in a game this season after being placed on injured reserve ahead of the Week 1 opener. Once he does return to action, Moore will provide depth behind Joey Porter (ankle), DaRon Bland, Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer already confirmed Monday that Goodson would be sidelined for multiple weeks due to the injury, and now that details have emerged regarding the severity of the issue, it's conceivable that the 26-year-old could be headed for injured reserve. The loss of Goodson leaves the Cowboys with no healthy running backs on the active roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but team owner Jerry jones said that the team plans to sign a free-agent back Tuesday, per Archer. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as backfield options on the practice squad.

Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3, despite playing 77 of 79 offensive snaps. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy now has reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Ezeiruaku suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Colts and didn't return. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the 49ers, Ezeiruaku may not be able to suit up for that one. If that's the case, Von Miller and Marist Liufau could see more snaps.

Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the season thus far, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine contests.

Locke suffered a concussion in Week 8 versus the Cardinals. While he was cleared to play in Week 9 against the Colts, he suffered another concussion. Now, Locke will miss at least one game, though the team will presumably be overly cautious before allowing him to get back on the field, meaning Markquese Bell may be in line for more snaps.

At a minimum, Ferguson is on track to miss at least this coming weekend's game against the 49ers, but a 'multiple week' timetable hints at a possible IR stint for the tight end. Next up for the Cowboy's reps at the position are Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) -- when healthy -- and James Mitchell. With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, it's also not difficult to imagine Dallas looking into gaining additional help in Ferguson's looming absence.

Aubrey was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game, but he did miss a kick for the second straight week. The kicker had makes from 45 and 28 yards in the contest, but he continued his long-range struggles Sunday, pulling a 50-yard attempt wide left late in the fourth quarter. Aubrey has now gone 17-for-22 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests to open the 2026 campaign.

Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.

Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

Winters was evaluated for a concussion earlier in the second half but was ultimately cleared to return. That's a big boost to Dallas' defense, especially since fellow linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) was unable to suit up Sunday.

Liufau broke his left forearm in the Cowboys' preseason finale against the Saints and has yet to play in the 2026 regular season. The linebacker is set to make his debut in Sunday's contest after being activated from IR on Saturday.

Bullard had his practice window opened Oct. 29 and was a full participant in all three of the Cowboys' practices this week. However, he's not yet ready to return to game action. Bullard's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco.

Singleton's six stops were a season low, but he still finished second on the Broncos in that category behind Jahdae Barron (eight). It's been a career year for Singleton, who is up to an NFL-leading 107 total tackles through nine regular-season games, which includes 2.0 sacks.

Trautman failed to record a catch across six games between Weeks 2 and 7, but he has logged two receptions in each of his two outings. His 41 offensive snaps ended up being ahead of fellow tight end Evan Engram (38), although the latter has been more involved in the Broncos' offensive game plan than Trautman. The Broncos' next game takes place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Nineteen of Mims' 24 snaps came on offense, although he logged only two touches in the process. He hasn't seen more than four targets in a game this season, with most of his output coming on special teams as a returner on both kickoffs and punts. The Broncos are on a bye for Week 10, so their next game will take place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22

Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.
Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 26 and 48 yards. The 32-year-old has now converted 16 of his 19 field-goal attempts and all 16 of his extra-point tries across nine appearances this season.
