With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "He'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

Coleman logged just 11 offensive snaps, and he's settled back in as the Dolphins' fourth receiver with all three of Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell healthy ahead of him on the depth chart. Coleman, a fifth-round rookie out of Missouri has no fantasy appeal.

This move was anticipated after Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps in Sunday's Week 9 loss to the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle is scheduled for surgery and will finish his ninth NFL campaign with 24 tackles, including 2.0 sacks. Zeek Biggers, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips could all take on more defensive snaps with Sieler sidelined for the rest of the season.

A 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles, McCord will be making his NFL debut Sunday, after he had been active for each of the 1-7 Dolphins' first eight games but didn't see any playing time behind Willis. Before landing with the Dolphins in a trade prior to Week 1, the 24-year-old signal-caller looked sharp during preseason action as a member of the Packers, completing 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT while adding 16 yards on five carries over three games. Expectations should still be held in check for McCord in his first regular-season action, especially while he'll be working with one of the NFL's weaker collections of skill-position players. The Dolphins are optimistic that Willis will be able to return from IR before the end of the season, but McCord should be primed for at least a four-game run as the team's starter while Willis is sidelined.

Miami now has used the maximum three standard elevations on Gonzalez, who has converted five of seven field-goal attempts and all five point-after attempts since joining the team. The Dolphins will need to sign Gonzalez to the 53-man roster if he's going to keep handling kicking duties in future weeks.

Allen's catch came on a fake punt, so it was an outlier of a play. He played just six offensive snaps behind clear RB1 Ollie Gordon. Since joining Miami via waivers last month, Allen has logged 31 snaps on special teams and six on offense. He has no fantasy appeal.

Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.

Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions, receiving yards and targets, as the rookie third-round pick continued to profile as one of Malik Willis' most reliable targets. Douglas' catch and target totals were also new career highs, while his yardage tally tied for the second highest of his nascent NFL tenure. Douglas should continue to play a key role in Miami's air attack over the second half of the season as the Dolphins look to continue cultivating their young talent.

Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and unsurprisingly he's trending toward being immediately installed as the starter, as his new team is in the midst of a two-game skid. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) viewed as week-to-week,  Carson Wentz (ankle, limited at practice Thursday) -- if available -- and Max Brosmer profile as his Week 10 backup options. Prior to being dealt, Cousins was playing well for Las Vegas, and his addition to the Minnesota offense should result in a boost for the team's top pass catchers, Justin Jefferson, T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison.

Cashman was injured in the Week 9 meeting with the Bills. He missed practice for a second consecutive day, so his chances of suiting up in Week 10 against the Packers don't appear to be high. If Cashman is ruled out for that contest, Ivan Pace could see more snaps.

Jennings was estimated as a non-participant on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9, and he wasn't able to take the practice field Thursday. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably end up missing a second straight game in Week 10, which could leave Myles Price with an expanded role at wideout come Sunday at Green Bay.

Wentz had his left ankle stepped on by Vikings left guard Joe Huber during Monday's loss to the Bills, and while he didn't miss a snap before Max Brosmer took over for the final possession, the former has operated with practice restrictions to begin Week 10 prep. With the acquisition of Kirk Cousins on Tuesday and Kyler Murray still week to week due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Wentz is expected to return to a reserve role Sunday at Green Bay, but head coach Kevin O'Connell hasn't announced a starter for that contest as of Thursday.

Hockenson now has logged back-to-back DNPs to begin Week 10 prep as he tends to wrist and chest injuries. The Vikings may make a ruling on the tight end's status as soon as they post their final practice report of the week Friday, but if Hockenson is inhibited to sidelined Sunday at Green Bay, Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew are the next players up at the position.

The veteran linebacker has started all eight games this season, logging 94 percent of the defensive snaps for Minnesota. He's now up to 50 tackles (24 solo), including 3.0 sacks, seven QB hits and a pass breakup. He's been extremely productive under defensive coordinator Brian Flores over the last two seasons, recording 9.5 sacks as an off-bal linebacker across 25 regular-season games during that span.

Murray already has missed one game due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain and is expected to be sidelined longer as the Vikings begin prep for Sunday's game at Green Bay. Minnesota acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, but O'Connell wasn't ready to commit to him as the team's Week 10 starting QB as of Wednesday. Assuming Murray is out again this weekend, Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer will be the signal-caller options at O'Connell's disposal.

Jefferson averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 yards and 8.5 touchdowns. Though Cousins is three years older than when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and working with an underwhelming receiver group. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

Felton continues to handle a muted role as a depth receiver for Minnesota, as Monday marked the third consecutive game in which he played single-digit snaps. For the season, the second-year wideout out of Maryland has been limited to just three receptions for 41 yards on seven targets over eight appearances.

Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

Price wasn't the only Minnesota pass catcher who logged an inefficient line, as starting quarterback Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 pass attempts. Price did make an impact in the return game by averaging 31.0 yards on his four kickoff returns. Price's role continues to be mostly centered on special teams, as he's caught just four passes for 32 yards on 11 targets through eight games.

After missing his lone field-goal attempt in Week 8 against the Lions, Reichard bounced back Monday to connect on field goals from 43 and 53 yards in the second quarter, which ended up being the only points that the Vikings scored. Reichard's 20 made field goals through eight regular-season games is tied for fourth-most in the NFL, and his seven makes from 50-plus yards is tied with Ka'imi Fairbairn for second behind Spencer Shrader (eight). The Vikings are 6-2 despite their struggles on offense this season, but the acquisition of Kirk Cousins should help make the unit more efficient. Minnesota will travel to Lambeau Field for Week 10 against Green Bay on Nov. 15.

Brosmer replaced Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game after the offense failed to produce a touchdown drive. Week 9 was Brosmer's first appearance in a 2026 regular-season game. He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.

Addison finished third in receptions and receiving yards on the night for a low-volume Vikings passing game, and his final catch, which went for 16 yards, came on Minnesota's last drive from the arm of Max Brosmer. Carson Wentz's game-long ineffectiveness depressed the production of the air attack as a whole, but Addison would be in better position to boost his numbers if Kyler Murray (hamstring) is able to return for Sunday's Week 10 road matchup against the Packers.

Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.
Levi Drake Rodriguez, Elijah Williams and Jalen Redmond will handle more of the defensive-line duties with Ingram-Dawkins sidelined.

Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.

Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

Jackson did not practice Thursday and Friday. While he practiced in a limited capacity Saturday, it still wasn't enough to avoid a questionable designation. However, Jackson has since been upgraded and is ready to go versus the Bills.

Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.

Though Henry was limited at practice all three days leading up to the contest, the Patriots were likely managing his reps in anticipation of having the tight end available this weekend. While it's possible that the team will get top WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) back versus Detroit, RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is still out and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, questionable) is banged up, so Henry figures to be a key available option for QB Drake Maye to work with, provided he avoids any setbacks with his foot.

Despite a report earlier in the week indicating that Stevenson would likely miss some time, the running back's ability to log limited practices both Thursday and Friday gives him a chance to play this weekend. With a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled, those considering Stevenson or A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) in Week 10 fantasy lineups, the duo's status will be know before the first wave of games Sunday. Moreover, there's a pretty good chance that NFL insiders such as Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network and Adam Schefter of ESPN will provide some updates on New England's injury situation either late Saturday or early Sunday. If the team ends up holding Stevenson out ahead of a Week 11 bye, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next in line for backfield work versus Detroit this weekend, with with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) still sidelined.

The same applies to RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), with coach Mike Vrabel having said "pretty good" when asked before Friday's practice about his view on how the duo was progressing toward playing this weekend. Fortunately for those considering Brown (who was listed as limited at practice Wednesday through Friday) in Week 10 fantasy lineups, his status will be known before the first wave of games Sunday, with a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled.

On the topic of when the running back might return, Vrabel noted Friday, "when that is, I don't know. I don't have a timetable." Henderson, who last saw game action in Week 7, has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions, and based on Vrabel's statement, the 2025 second-rounder's status beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye is unclear. Fellow RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) returned to a limited practice Thursday, but if he ends up being held out this weekend, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next up for the team's backfield work versus Detroit, with Terrell Jennings representing a possible practice squad elevation.

Gonzalez's 10 stops were a season high, but the larger concern was his poor performance in coverage. Per Pro Football Focus, Gonzalez was on coverage for 11 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and quarterback Jordan Love had a 158.3 passing rating while targeting the fourth-year defensive back. It wasn't the performance that the Patriots were expecting after signing Gonzalez to a lucrative four-year, $135 million contract extension in September. Things won't get easier for him or the Patriots' secondary, as they travel to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions, whose offense ranks fourth in the NFL in yards per game (379.8).

Campbell suffered a knee injury against the Packers in Week 9, but he was cleared to practice in full Wednesday. Given his full practice reps, Campbell should start at left tackle Sunday against the Lions in Munich.

Woods was unable to play against the Packers in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. He's opened Week 10 prep with a limited practice, and if he's cleared to play Sunday against the Lions in Munich, then he would be a candidate for more work in the secondary due to the absence of Carlton Davis (knee).

Brown tweaked his knee against the Packers in Week 9, and the injury is severe enough for him to not travel with the team to Munich. In his absence, Walter Rouse is expected to serve as the Patriots' starter at left guard. Since the Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, Brown's next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Byard was working through a chest injury in October, but it's unclear whether he's dealing with the same issue for the start of Week 10 prep. The veteran safety will have two more chances to increase his practice participation before the Patriots travel to Munich to face the Lions on Sunday. Byard has 43 tackles (23 solo) and three pass defenses (including one interception) through the first nine games of the regular season.

Davis suffered a knee injury during the Patriots' loss to the Packers this past Sunday. New England already ruled out the veteran defensive back for Week 10, so Charles Woods (hamstring), Channing Canada and Karon Prunty figure to be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Davis will have more time to recover for Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The fullback hasn't played since Week 4. He's logged 58 snaps on offense and another 39 on special teams across four appearances this season.

Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.

Borregales didn't attempt a field goal, and it was the second time this season that he didn't kick any. For the year, the second-year kicker in 10 of 13 on FGAs and has made 23 of 24 extra points. He'll be a fantasy target for next Sunday's potential shootout in Detroit.

TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

Maye was constantly harassed by an aggressive Packers defense that sacked him four times for 27 total yards in losses while also repeatedly getting hands on his throws. Working with a receiving corps that welcomed back Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve but was still down A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder), Maye threw his first interception on the second play of the game on a deep pass intended for Hollins, and his other two picks came during the second quarter. Two of the three INTs led to Green Bay touchdowns, and after throwing just eight interceptions over 17 regular-season games in 2025, Maye is up to 11 over nine contests this season following Sunday's game. The third-year signal-caller's first chance to atone comes in a Week 10 matchup against a seemingly improved Lions defense in Munich, Germany, next Sunday.

After missing four weeks on injured reserve with a calf injury, Hollins returned to the lineup Sunday and immediately became a central part of the offense, tying Kyle Williams for second on the team with 34 routes on 46 dropbacks by New England's quarterbacks. Hollins' six targets also tied Eli Raridon for second on the team behind DeMario Douglas' nine. With A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) still not 100 percent, Hollins figures to remain a big part of the picture next Sunday against the Lions in a potential shootout under the dome at Ford Field.

Chism was able to reel in exactly five passes for the second straight week, and he connected with quarterback Drake Maye for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The score was Chism's second of the year and first since Week 4. With A.J. Brown (knee) potentially set to miss the team's Week 10 matchup against the Lions, Chism may have a chance to operate in a prominent role again against Detroit's underwhelming secondary.

Fuaga was a new addition to the Saints' injury report Thursday, suggesting he may have gotten hurt at practice. In any case, he'll probably need to manage a full practice Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

Edwards popped up on the Saints' injury report Wednesday with a knee injury, and now his status for Week 10 looks uncertain. He might have to practice in full Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Banks was able to play in Week 9 after the Saints activated him from injured reserve, but his ankle still seems to be bothering him ahead of Sunday's game versus the Panthers. If he can't upgrade to a full practice Friday, he may get stuck with an injury designation going into the weekend.
questionable

Fant was limited at Wednesday's practice, but the veteran TE faced no limitations Thursday, suggesting that he'll be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He has worked as the Saints' No. 2 option at the position behind Juwan Johnson.

Donaldson has yet to resume practicing since sustaining a shoulder injury in Week 7, which suggests he's trending for another absence in Sunday's Week 10 matchup with the Panthers. Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are both expected to be available, while Travis Etienne's (hamstring) status is up in the air as the latter tries to work his way back from a hamstring injury that landed him on IR.

Kamara was listed as a non-participant Wednesday due to the combination of rest and back, but his return to all drills one day later gives him the all-clear ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Panthers. He may be welcoming back fellow RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) in Week 10 after the latter was designated for return from IR and so far has managed a pair of limited sessions, while Audric Estime is coming off a 16-touch showing this past Sunday versus the Browns.

The Saints designated Etienne for return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he so far has logged back-to-back limited practices during Week 10 prep. He'll have one more opportunity Friday to put himself in a position for his first game action since Week 3, when he suffered a strained left hamstring.

Werner co-led the Saints in tackles in Week 9, and it was the third time he's reached double-digit stops over his last four outings. Werner is on pace to record his first 100-plus tackle campaign of his six-year NFL career and is up to 65 tackles (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

Granderson took down Shedeur Sanders for sacks of six and nine yards in the second and third quarters, respectively. Granderson has logged at least 1.5 sacks in each of his last four outings, and his 7.5 sacks on the year are tied for fourth-most in the NFL and one shy from matching his career high in 2023. The Saints will stay home for Week 10 against the Panthers and Bryce Young, who has been sacked 26 times, which is fourth-most in the NFL.

Elliss entered Week 9 without a sack to his name, but he changed that early in the first quarter after taking down Shedeur Sanders for a seven-yard loss. Elliss' 11 stops co-led the Saints, and the veteran linebacker is up to 41 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense across five regular-season games.

Tyson played just 18 snaps and lost a fumble on his first catch this past Sunday against the Browns, but there were some positives from his regular-season debut, including a strong target rate (five targets on 16 routes). While there's no assurance of a full-time role, Tyson at least figures to take more snaps away from fellow rookie Bryce Lance, if not from veteran Devaughn Vele.

Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season NFL debut against Cleveland, Lance saw his snaps cut against Cleveland. After playing 79 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 7 against Pittsburgh, Lance logged just 51 percent of the plays versus the Browns. He has nine catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets this season.

Smyth was elevated ahead of Sunday's Week 9 overtime win over Cleveland. He served as New Orleans' kicker in the contest and went 3-for-4 on FGAs while making both of his PAT attempts. That performance was likely good enough for Smyth to be elevated again for this Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.

With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

Per Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio New Orleans, Moore also said Monday that McCoy is not tending to a long-term or season-ending injury, and he does not believe it will require surgery. William Sherman filled in for McCoy at center after he exited during the fourth quarter in Week 9, but Cesar Ruiz also has experience at the position, and rookie fourth-rounder Jeremiah Wright is available should the Saints need him at guard.

Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

The star wideout finished with less than 50 receiving yards for the second time in five days, and Nabers' late third-quarter lost fumble had significant ramifications. The turnover came at the Commanders' 16-yard line with the Giants down by three, costing  New York a golden opportunity to tie the game at minimum. Nabers' aforementioned pair of mediocre performances have come in the wake of a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts in Weeks 4-7, and he'll look to boost his numbers back up against the Jaguars' pass-funnel defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Skattebo put together an impressive all-around performance that included a season high in receiving yards. He also exceeded the 75-yard mark on the ground for the third time on the campaign, and he went in for his third and fourth rushing touchdowns of the season on one- and 13-yard runs in the first and third quarters, respectively. Skattebo didn't show any ill effects from the hamstring injury that cost him Sunday's win over the Eagles, and he'll now gear up for a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars' elite run defense on Sunday, Nov. 22.

Pinnock exited the game early in the third quarter with a back injury, and his status for the rest of the game is uncertain. In his absence, Tyler Nubin will be thrust into a more prominent role in New York's secondary.

Harrison was limited at practice throughout the week and has since been ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with the Commanders. The 28-year-old has played sparingly on defense during the 2026 campaign, though his absence will be felt on special teams. Harrison's next opportunity to suit up will come in Week 11 versus Jacksonville.

Singletary recorded a season-high 23 touches in Skattebo's absence during the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9 but mustered only 39 yards with all that volume. Prior to that win, Singletary hadn't exceeded six carries in a game this season. Skattebo is expected to lead the backfield in his return, with Singletary likely to feature in passing situations since Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) remains on IR. Greg Desrosiers is also on the roster at RB.

McFadden jumped on a fumble caused by Arvell Reese's sack of Joe Milton early in the second quarter, and McFadden logged a sack of his own -- his first of the 2026 regular season -- early in the third quarter. The fifth-year pro has accumulated 19 total tackles over his last two games, which has coincided with his move to a starting role due to Tremaine Edmunds (chest) being on injured reserve.

The Giants' pass rush made life miserable for Eagles quarterback Joe Milton, who was making his first start of the season in Week 9. Reese was responsible for three of the Giants' seven sacks, including a strip sack early in the second quarter that caused a takeaway. It was the second time in 2026 that Reese logged double-digit tackles, and he is up to 68 tackles (49 solo), including 4.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through eight regular-season games.

Carter logged limited practices Monday and Tuesday before upgrading to full practice Wednesday. Across eight starts this season, the No. 3 overall pick of the 2025 Draft has produced 19 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble. He has yet to develop into a game-wrecking edge rusher.

Desrosiers made his regular-season debut during the victory, serving as the team's No. 2 running back behind Devin Singletary, as Cam Skattebo was out due to a hamstring injury. With Skattebo now healthy again, Desrosiers will likely be relegated to a depth role during Thursday's matchup versus the Commanders.

Hood left Tuesday's practice with a trainer after injuring his finger, but Harbaugh told reporters after the session that the rookie second-rounder will "be fine." It's possible that Hood doesn't miss any game time, although Wednesday's injury report will shed light on his status for Thursday's NFC East tilt against the Commanders. Most of his playing time has been on special teams, but Hood's absence would give the Giants less depth in the secondary.

The tight end played just 12 offensive snaps, logging a 17.9 percent snap share against Philly. On the season, Johnson has just four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown on nine targets across six appearances. He has no fantasy appeal with Isaiah Likely healthy.

Listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice, Mooney took every rep a day later to erase any concern about his status heading into Thursday's game against the Commanders. The veteran wideout has played more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in all but one of the Giants' eight games to date, but he exceeded two receptions and 50 receiving yards for the first time all season in this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. He remains a relatively unappealing fantasy option while receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely are locked in as the Giants' clear top two pass catchers.

After Zvada missed both of his field-goal tries in the Giants' pre-Week 8 bye overtime win over the Texans two weeks ago, coach John Harbaugh stuck with the rookie kicker, and Zvada answered with a perfect afternoon against Philly. Zvada accounted for 13 of the team's 19 points, converting field goals from 53, 49, 38 and 49 yards. On the season, he's 17-for-22 on field-goal tries and 13-for-13 on PATs.

After logging limited practices earlier in the week, Cooper may avoid an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with the Bills. Fellow Jets wideout Garrett Wilson (concussion) also has a chance to be cleared before Sunday, as he's upgrading to full practice participation Friday along with Cooper.

Wilson will upgrade to full participation Friday after logging limited practices earlier in the week. He's on track to return after missing just one game, but he'll still need clearance from a neurologist if Friday's practice goes as planned.
out

Bailey had a productive outing despite the loss as he was the only Jets defender to record a sack. The 23-year-old has gotten off to a strong start during his rookie campaign, compiling 34 tackles (26 solo), including 7.5 sacks, and five forced fumbles across his first eight games.

The Jets only held a walkthrough practice Wednesday, and they projected that Phillips would not have been able to practice at all if a standard session had taken place. He'll likely need to get back on the practice field in a full capacity Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Wright was out in Week 9 because of his back injury, and his status for Week 10 is now up in the air as well. He'll probably need to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

Ossai has missed the Jets' last four games while recovering from an ankle injury. He's been able to practice in a limited capacity, but he may need to log a full session in order to be cleared to play against the Bills on Sunday.

Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.

Reeder is returning to New York after having been released by the Jets in October. The 32-year-old has logged four tackles (one solo) across six outings this season and will likely continue to see the majority of his playing time come on special teams during his second tenure with the Jets.

The 2023 first-round pick racked up 18.5 sacks over the previous two seasons and has three on his ledger through nine games in 2026, but he's seen his playing time tail off with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick David Bailey and the addition of Kingsley Enagbare in free agency. Though McDonald is hopeful to land with a team that can present him with a clearer path to a full-time role, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that McDonald "is going to be here" once the deadline passes, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.

Sanders provided all the offense for New York in Week 9, making exactly four field goals for the second straight week and third time in the last four contests. The kicker converted attempts from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards before pulling his lone miss wide left from 53 yards, all of which came in the first half. Sanders has now gone 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now gone without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.

After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.

Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.

Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.

Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.

Belton was able to secure double-digit stops for the second time this season, finishing second on the team behind linebacker Jamien Sherwood (14). Belton is now up to 68 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding four passes defensed over eight contests to begin the regular season.

Sherwood notched a season-high 14 takedowns in the victory, securing double-digit stops for the third time in the last five contests. The linebacker has now compiled 68 total tackles (32 solo), four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.

Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

Earlier Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relayed that the Eagles agreed to send Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade wasn't cancelled due to concerns over Ebiketie's physical; instead, the Bengals opted to call it off since they would have lost a third-round compensatory pick if the deal was completed, per Rapoport. The Eagles could still look to move Ebiketie elsewhere prior to Tuesday's deadline, but barring another trade, he'll suit up for Philadelphia in its Week 10 game against Pittsburgh.

Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

Elliott's kick was good from 45 yards, but with Joe Milton making his first start at quarterback and without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), the Philly offense struggled to move the ball and score points. Elliott is not an exciting fantasy kicker on a tanking Eagles team.

The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

Baun exited the second half of Sunday's game with a back injury. Smael Mondon will fill in at inside linebacker opposite Jeremiah Trotter while Baun receives further medical evaluation to determine if he can return to the contest.
McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

Smith was a full participant in Friday's practice, and he was cleared from the league's concussion protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa.

Elliott had no injury designation in practice Thursday after popping up as a limited participant in practice Wednesday. The 29-year-old has played just two games through nine weeks of the NFL regular season. He returned from injured reserve in Week 7, totaling two tackles (two solo) on the season.

Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

Echols missed the last two games before Pittsburgh's bye in Week 9 because of a hamstring injury, but it looks like he's on track to be available in Week 10. Through six games so far in 2026, a substantial majority of his snaps have come on special teams.

Slaughter was unable to play against the Browns in Week 8 due to a hamstring injury that prevented him from practicing. His ability to log a full session Wednesday puts him on track to play against the Bengals on Sunday, when he's expected to play mostly on special teams while providing the Steelers depth in the secondary.

Skowronek was sidelined by a calf injury for the Steelers' three games prior to the Week 9 bye. His full practice participation Wednesday indicates that he is fully recovered from the injury and will suit up for Sunday's contest against the Browns. Skowronek has three catches on four targets for 32 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.

Harmon said he's 100 percent healthy, but the team will take things day-to-day with the defensive lineman, according to Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com. Harmon hasn't played since Week 4. He's recorded 12 tackles (three solo), including 1.5 sacks, across 85 defensive snaps this season.

Boswell missed a 57-yard attempt on the Steelers' first offensive drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to nail 20-yard and 37-yard attempts en route to five straight made kicks. Boswell is now 18-for-23 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-16 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.

Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.

Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.

Jaylen Warren spearheaded the Steelers' attack with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score of his own. When combined with a highly effective effort by Pittsburgh's defense, there wasn't much production required of Rodgers and the air attack after much busier games leading into Sunday. Rodgers finished with season-low figures in completions, pass attempts, completion percentage and passing yards while failing to throw a touchdown pass for the first time since Week 2, but he's highly likely to revert to his prior pass-heavy ways in a Week 10 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday night, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

Smith had already been elevated from the practice squad thrice, so Saturday's move means he's eligible to suit up for the Steelers for the rest of the season. The Iowa product caught both of his targets for 24 yards against the Saints in Week 7. If Ben Skowronek (calf) cannot play Sunday, then Smith, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Johnson would all be in line for more offensive snaps.

Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.

Queen had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles in addition to registering his first sack of the campaign. The 2020 first-round pick has now logged 48 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across seven games this season.

Rudolph has emerged as the Steelers' preferred backup quarterback behind starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers coming out of the preseason. Through each of Pittsburgh's first seven contests, Rudolph has suited up, while both Will Howard and Drew Allar have been inactive. Howard is the Steelers' emergency No. 3 quarterback and will be called upon to play only in the event that both Rodgers and Rudolph are forced to exit Sunday's game.

Watt was limited by a calf injury Thursday, but he's good to go for Pittsburgh's Paris game against New Orleans. Through six games this season, the 32-year-old Watt has 15 tackles (10 solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and a pick-six interception.

Williams presumably sustained a shoulder injury in Week 9 versus the Raiders, and now his availability for Week 10 is in some doubt. If he can't log a full practice Friday, there's a chance he could end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Greenlaw had eight tackles in Sunday's win over the Raiders. While he was limited Thursday, he has more time to get cleared to suit up versus the Cowboys in Week 10. If Greenlaw can't get on the field, Jaden Dugger and Garret Wallow are both in line for more snaps.

Shanahan's comments signal the 49ers are taking an extra cautious approach with the veteran wideout in the hopes that he'll be available down the home stretch of the season. While Evans hasn't officially been ruled out for Sunday's game at Dallas, he isn't expected to suit up in Week 10, per Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site. Until he's fully recovered and ready to go again, his absence should continue to open up additional opportunities outside for 2025 fourth-rounder Jordan Watkins.

Samuel has managed back-to-back capped sessions to kick off Week 10 prep as he vies for his first game action since Week 5 at Seattle, when he injured his right hamstring. Friday's injury report will reveal his odds to suit up Sunday in Dallas.

Dugger set the tone for the 49ers right out of halftime, when he intercepted a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tre Tucker and returned it 35 yards for a pick-six for the first defensive touchdown of Dugger's young NFL career. The rookie fifth-rounder has logged at least six solo tackles in three of his last four games and is up to 36 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pick-six through eight regular-season games.

Warner's five stops tied a season low, although he did recover the fumble late in the third quarter that the 49ers' offense converted into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to Jordan Watkins seven plays later. Warner has played every single defensive snap in each of the 49ers' last six games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 77 tackles (36 solo), including 0.5 sacks, three pass defenses, five forced fumbles and one fumble recovery through eight regular-season games.

The 49ers opened West's 21-day practice window Wednesday, and he was limited in his return to on-field practice. He landed on injured reserve in late September due to a knee injury, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Cowboys.

Lenoir is considered day-to-day due to a foot injury that he picked up in Week 9 against the Raiders. He was an observer for Wednesday's session, and he'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's tilt against the Cowboys. Lenoir has accumulated 33 tackles (20 solo) and one pass defense through eight regular-season games.

Green injured his back in the second half of the 49ers' win over the Raiders in Week 9, and he finished that game with four tackles (two solo) and one interception. Per Barrows, head coach Kyle Shanahan indicated Monday that Green is considered day-to-day, so the third-year defensive back's practice participation over the next two days will determine whether he'll be available for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

injuries.evidence: Halton suffered a broken left ankle in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over Las Vegas and is out for the season.
injuries.detail: Halton suffered a broken left ankle in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over Las Vegas and is out for the season. The fourth-round rookie finished his inaugural NFL campaign with 15 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, a defensed pass, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery (which he returned for a touchdown) over eight contests. San Francisco's recent acquisition of DeForest Buckner softens the blow of losing Halton a bit.

Cooks and other 49ers wide receivers operated in elevated roles Sunday due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 25 receiving yards ended up being third-most on the Niners behind Jordan Watkins (86) and tight end George Kittle (58), and Cooks' 32 offensive snaps were also third-most among San Francisco wide receivers. The 49ers hit the road for Week 10 against the Cowboys, and Cooks' workload on offense figures to decrease with Keenan Allen now in the fold, and with Evans or Samuel potentially ready to return.

Playing in his first game since Week 2 due to a high ankle sprain, Robinson played 51 percent of the Niners' offensive snaps against Las Vegas. San Francisco's wideout situation is a week-to-week thing moving forward, with the Tuesday addition of Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all likely to return at some point in the near future. Robinson isn't someone to roster in 12-team fantasy leagues.

Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.

A beat-up 49ers receiving corps will get some much-needed reinforcement in the form of Allen, who has still displayed the ability to move the chains during his age-34 season. Through eight games with the Colts, Allen produced a 40-351-1 receiving line on 58 targets. While Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) may be prioritized ahead of him in the passing game once fully healthy, Allen could have the opportunity to see steady target volume right out of the gate Sunday in Dallas.

As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.

Pineiro continues to see the majority of his action handling extra-point duties, as he's now attempted just two field goals across his last three outings and only 10 total on the season. Sunday's performance also marked just the second time this season that the 31-year-old didn't miss a kick.

In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

Black led the 49ers in rushing yards, finishing with two more than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey operated as the clear lead back and scored twice on 20 touches. McCaffrey won't be unseated as the starter while healthy, but Black has started to earn a larger role, with double-digit carries for at least 63 rushing yards in consecutive games. The rookie third-round pick is averaging a solid 4.5 yards per carry heading into a Week 10 road game against the Cowboys.

Watkins set a new career high in receiving yards, thanks in large part to a 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, which was the first of his NFL career. He has taken on a larger role over the past two games during the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), as Watkins had 56 receiving yards on six targets to lead San Francisco's wide receivers in Week 7 prior to the team's Week 8 bye. If at least one of Evans or Samuel remains sidelined in Week 10, Watkins would be poised to maintain an expanded role against a weak Dallas defense.

Cross hasn't been able to get onto the field since suffering a high ankle sprain back in Week 7 versus the Chiefs, but he took a big step in the right direction by returning to practice Thursday. With that said, he'll probably need to upgrade to full participation at practice Friday to have a realistic chance at suiting up Sunday at Las Vegas.

Lock continues to deal with a right elbow injury, and he's also tending to an oblique issue that he suffered this past Sunday against the Cardinals. He discussed the new health concern Thursday, telling Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle that he's "feeling good" and the oblique injury is on his backside, which is easier to deal with than if it was on the lead side. Lock so far has had his practice reps capped this week as a result, and Friday's injury report will determine if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas.

Jones finished tied for second on the team in tackles behind Julian Love during Sunday's victory. Jones has now racked up seven or more tackles in all nine of his outings to start the season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Raiders.

Hall only played 29 of the Seahawks' 53 defensive snaps in Week 9 versus the Cardinals, and the fact that he's dealing with a back injury might be part of the reason why. He'll probably have to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

Williams was sidelined for Sunday's game versus the Cardinals due to a shoulder injury, and now his status for Week 10 is in question. He'll likely need to return to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday to put himself on track to play Sunday at Las Vegas.

Shaheed suffered a knee injury during a Week 7 win against the Chiefs and missed the last two games as a result. Now that he's unhindered on the practice field, though, he'll resume his standing as Seattle's No. 2 WR and primary kick and punt returner

Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), but Lock is now dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the floors for Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.
